2611.06321.image_caption: Fig. 1 | | The dual-loop structure of EnzymeRSI. a , Dual-loop recursive self-improvement. The outer loop evolves versions of prompts, pipelines, skills and subagents, which are adopted or rolled back after diagnosis, a minimal consistent change bundle and a paired comparison at matched budget; model weights are not modified. The inner loop is triggered only when a method bottleneck appears, and develops predictors, training strategies, search operators and acquisition functions under controlled conditions. Missing packages and permission problems are handled as engineering faults and trigger neither loop. Adoption rules are fixed before the comparison as global adoption, scoped retention or rollback, and an adopted version must be loaded by the next run. The protein, algorithm and system tiers are scored independently and are not collapsed into a single weighted number (Section 4.7). Evidence and Trajectory record measurements, QC status, sample identity, batch, references, checksums of raw files and execution receipts, and return along the sequence evidence, hypothesis, action, result, decision. They may trigger either loop or neither. The legend distinguishes three arrow types: a black arrow is an accepted revision, an orange arrow is experiment flow and a green dashed arrow is evidence or a trigger, which is used as required. b , Cloud Lab. Candidates that have been scored in dry-lab evaluation and passed ProtoPilot–Operon-S1 fast decisions form a wet-lab commission, which runs on the adopted version, is orchestrated by ProtoPilot and compiled into device tasks, and is then scheduled, measured and quality-controlled by the execution layer. The same task contract can address a single instrument, a workcell, a production line or a cloud laboratory. A receipt evidences a software event only; an actual transfer requires measurement and QC support. A sample that passes QC but shows low activity is valid evidence, whereas a failed run enters execution diagnosis. Measurements return to Evidence and Trajectory.

2611.06381.image_caption: Figure 1: Task description and main pipeline of LegalEvolver.

2611.06542.image_caption: Figure 1: Motivation for adapting PI acquisition. (a) White-box distillation uses accessible teacher logits for token-level supervision; black-box distillation uses teacher text for SeqKD or reward-based training. (b) Four fixed PI acquisition strategies evaluated on AIME 2025 and 2026 (16 samples per question). Left: unassisted accuracy along separate training trajectories. Right: unassisted accuracy after training from each GRPO parent checkpoint on the same data for two epochs (20 additional data steps and 80 optimizer updates); gray crosses mark parent-model accuracy before branch training. Strategy rankings change with student state.

2611.06654.image_caption: Figure 1: Architecture of Compounding Physical RSI. Closed-loop execution in RoboDojo-Sim feeds automated stage-level capability-gap assessment (Diagnosis), which produces a structured objective g k g_{k} to guide experience curation and offline reinforcement learning (Remedy). Retention interpolates candidates between the inherited reference policy and the refined policy, promotes the best-performing candidate via full-benchmark evaluation, and passes it forward as the reference state for the next generation.

2611.06768.image_caption: Figure 1 : PyRUA-REAL: Python-based Robot-Use Agents for Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning. (a) Coding agents iteratively explore, execute, diagnose, and revise robot programs, retaining rollout experience as persistent memory and reusable skills. (b) Development-stage improvements in success rate and cycle time, including reset, for stacking, tic-tac-toe, and Hanoi. (c) Real-world success rates aggregated over development attempts for seven agent-free skills. (d) RoboDojo performance compared with eight baselines, measured by success rate averaged equally over five capability groups. (e) The eight real-world tasks include semantic reasoning, precise manipulation, contact-rich manipulation, deformable object manipulation and long-horizon tasks.

2611.06244.image_caption: Figure 2 : Overview of Rubric Curriculum RL (RcRL). (Left) The challenge: training with a static rubric leads to reward hacking, where the model optimizes for the reward signal without improving true quality. (Right) Our solution: RcRL progressively introduces evaluation criteria, using pairwise comparisons to allocate rewards. The curriculum advances when current criteria have improved (Section 5.2 ).

2611.06343.image_caption: Figure 1: Capabilities of Prism. Prism improves both understanding and generation through self-teaching on interleaved text-image trajectories. The base model shows redundant steps on step 2 in the cooking tutorial, while Prism produces a coherent and correct tutorial. It also improves performance on standalone understanding and generation tasks.

2611.06414.image_caption: Figure 1: An illustrative exploration task modeled as a graph. We highlight two branches, whose exploration steps are interconnected by relations.

2611.06445.image_caption: (a) SumOne is a lightweight, standalone memory compressor applicable to diverse agents and tasks.

2611.06518.image_caption: Figure 2: EmoReward calibrates emotional evidence within videos and across training runs. Plan translates intent into evaluation criteria, and Act obtains provider scores and evidence validity. Reflect combines current-video gates with memory-derived multipliers and normalizes over active providers. Evolve estimates contextual reliability from a completed reference run to construct the fixed multipliers used in subsequent training. The calibrated emotion reward complements the original video reward; GRPO updates the generator while the providers and memory table remain frozen.

2611.06543.image_caption: Figure 1: The overview of ORSD. (a) For each task, the policy first samples a group of trajectories. It then takes the task description and these trajectories as inputs to generate multiple rubric bundles. (b) Each Rubric bundle is evaluated on every trajectory, the rubric bundle with the largest rubric-reward alignment score is selected. (c) The selected rubric bundle is used to augment the context and compute the per-token likelihood gap between augmented and non-augmented contexts, enabling per-token advantage shaping of the original trajectory-level advantage.

2611.06905.image_caption: Figure 8: Generalization across objects. Left: Training objects per MolmoSpaces split. Each split contains all objects of the previous one; + + marks objects added. The 1-task split is trained separately on a single box or spatula task. Full task details are in Table 3 . Right: We train each method on tasks involving a single object (box or spatula) and evaluate on the unseen knife. For methods that use a critic (BoN, OGPO), training on a similar object transfers better, whereas FSFT shows no such pattern. We report the mean and 95% stratified bootstrap CIs across three seeds.

2611.05450.image_caption: Figure 1: ReScopeBench overview. (a) Experience-first construction connects executable environments, discoverable dependencies, and verified task streams. (b) Agents acquire, reuse, and selectively revise experience after silent changes.

2611.05662.image_caption: Figure 1: Grounding does not immunize the judge. On an identical Postgres migration, a single false pre-screening cue (yellow) flips the verdict: both judges confirm all 200 200 rows migrated, but the cued judge defers to the “expert” and fails the run ( 0.70 0.70 vs. the uncued 0.99 0.99 ), a meta-judge attributes the flip to over-trust .

2611.06483.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of our findings. Left: Multi-turn agentic RL does not uniformly enhance per-step action quality; rather, it mainly enhances ability of error recovery and long-horizon resilience. Right: The trajectory-level gains of agentic RL depend on a sufficient interaction budget ( T T ).

2611.06803.image_caption: Figure 2: The 2-d Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS) induced with raw trace embeddings (top) and the trubric embeddings (bottom) under different numbers of reference systems and task executions. Each dot is a system colored by its full benchmark score on SWE-bench Verified. For a given setting, the manifold of systems induced by trubric embeddings is more predictive of the full benchmark score, as measured by MAE under the leave-one-system-out protocol.

2611.06841.image_caption: Figure 2 : Agents design the server and choose how many sessions it serves at once for a given model, GPU allocation, and workload. Replay preserves shared context and dependencies between requests; final checks assess model correctness and complete workload execution.

2611.06863.image_caption: Figure 2: Guidance improves recovery under fixed token budgets. (a) An initial failure followed by a successful retry after reset. (b) Recovery under total-token budgets. (c) Paired recovery@5 comparisons show an advantage over resampling, with no detected advantage over different-label or fixed-template guidance.

2611.06910.image_caption: Figure 9: The proposal of the example task. Top: proposal.pdf , the one-page brief that agent need to read first. It sets out the physics and the goal, and describe what are the questions should be answered after literature research. The last paragraph leaves four questions to the agent’s own research (numbered). Bottom: for each question, what the literature must supply.
